profile.headline: Backend Software Engineer | Relationship Builder | Problem Solver
profile.summary:
Principal Software Engineer working in Finance Tech (Java, MySQL, Spring Framework, JUnit) developing REST APIs for backend money movement orchestration as a member of multiple Agile crews to deliver quality applications within the banking industry.

Former nonprofit Program Manager where I had the pleasure of working directly with a wide range of professionals across Pittsburgh as they honed their leadership skills and utilized those skills to benefit the wider community.

positions.description: Managed and executed all pre-event details (Host Committee, speaker coordination, invitations, venue communication, etc.) related to the 2019 Champagne Luncheon & Alumni Connection Event – Leadership Pittsburgh Inc.’s largest alumni engagement event held each January.

positions.title: Program Manager
positions.description:
My responsibilities as Program Manager include tasks related to management, event-planning, resource development, and most importantly, relationship building. 

Responsible for the management and implementation, day-to-day operations, budget management and program performance analysis of both the Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) and the Leadership OnBoard (LOB) program. The LDI program engages 50+ of our region’s top emerging high-potential professionals each year from the corporate, civic and non-profit sectors in a unique, skills/capacities-based experience that is part of many organizations’ talent management strategy. Oversee and handle logistics of planning and implementing each session including: registration and attendee tracking, create and monitor detailed event agendas for program team, track and maintain annual programmatic budget, serve as principal contact to the 50+ program participants, and continually ensure program improvement via monthly programmatic analysis. 

Additionally, manage special projects for alumni engagement and development including board matching, the Executive Welcome program, and alumni gatherings including the Champagne Luncheon & Alumni Connection Event – Leadership Pittsburgh Inc.’s largest alumni engagement event held each January, each year producing a sell out event. Provides support to fundraising and development efforts in collaboration with the Resource Development Committee of the Board of Directors, as well as the President & CEO.

Develop the timeline, execution and visual creation for a complete website redesign replacing an antiquated site with a more modern, more functional, and more client-friendly website (www.lpinc.org)

Organizational information: this non-profit organization is designed to examine critical community issues, enhance civic engagement among the region’s leaders, and empower them to act on the regional agenda at the leadership level.

positions.title: Special Projects Assistant
positions.description:
As the Special Projects Assistant, my position was multifaceted. Provided operational and event management support (site logistics, catering, set-up, coordination, etc.) for the Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) Program. Served as the primary resource for LDI participants during their PopUp! Pittsburgh Campaign by providing guidance for event insurance, special events permits, police contracts, vendor sourcing, social media/website outreach and invitation logistics. 

Responsible for working with our partner, the Allegheny Conference on Community Development, to execute networking and information-sharing events for new Pittsburgh regional executives. 

Managed the planning and execution of our largest alumni engagement event, the Annual Alumni Connection Event & Champagne Lunch.

positions.title: Patient Monitor
positions.description: Maintained constant observation of patients that were under psychological evaluations (suicidal, drug addicts, dementia, etc.) at all times, accompanied patient for tests or procedures, operated communication devices (telephone and patient call system) and protected patient from self-harm and assist with daily activities.

volunteerExperiences.description:
The Penn State Dance Marathon (THON) is the largest student run philanthropy in the world and annual campaign to raise funds for pediatric cancer research and treatment at Penn State Hershey Children’s Hospital. For THON 2013, I served as 1 of 15 executive directors who led largest Penn State student organization. Through my position of Executive Family Relations Chairperson, I gained extensive student leadership, organization management, and communication experience. Assisted in the fundraising of $12.37 million for childhood cancer with the 2013 Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance Marathon (THON), the largest student-run philanthropy in the world. 

Responsible for providing year round assistance and support to The Four Diamonds Families by ensuring that they enjoy all of their THON experiences to the fullest. Served as the liaison to more than 300 families treated at Penn State Hershey Children’s Hospital who participated in THON. Oversaw planning and execution of 4 programs and 20 events for families and led efforts of 23 project managers and advised 350 student organizations regarding their involvement with participating families. Launched initiatives to expand pediatric cancer education for more than 15,000 THON volunteers and increase efficiency in programs.

Participated as a member of the advisory board convened to research, explore, and provide feedback to five Pittsburgh-based art organizations pertaining to their program/activity recruitment and marketing efforts.
